topics.topic: Module ownership of A17 store-file checks and lifecycle operations
questions: Which module owns A17's removal of the store temporary file, creation of a new store under that name, and rename into place: `configuration`, `store`, or `instance_lifecycle`?

Which A17 rules or rule parts are owned by `configuration`, `store` and `instance_lifecycle` for resolving the store path, removing the temporary store, creating and renaming a new store, opening and integrity-checking an existing store, checking its release version, and removing a newly made store after listener failure?

quotes:
The checks after them — the backup probe (`backups`), opening or making the store
(`store`) and the listeners — are run in rule 2's order by
`instance_lifecycle`, which calls this module first.

opening it for reading and
writing at start, or making a new, empty store of the release's version —
holding no record but M12 AuditSequence at 0, which the release's statements
make with the store, so `store` needs nothing from `audit_log` — under
the temporary name and renaming it once complete, after removing a leftover of
that name and no other file (A17 rule 5), and removing a store it made new
when the start then fails at a listener (A17 rule 2);

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the configured addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2);
judgement.why: State 3 assigns the fileless and path-policy checks to configuration, every SQLite and store-file lifecycle operation to store, and startup ordering plus rollback coordination to instance_lifecycle.

topics.topic: Module ownership of the backup-location startup writability probe and its temporary probe file lifecycle
questions: Which module performs A17's writable-backup-location probe and creates/removes its temporary file: `configuration`, `backups`, or `instance_lifecycle` calling `backups`?

Which module owns and performs A17's startup writability probe in the backup location, including naming, creating and removing the probe and reporting failure, while `configuration` is the primary owner of A17 and may not know the later `backups` module?

quotes:
Reading the environment (`runtime_settings`), opening or making the store
(`store`), probing the backup location (`backups`), what a token may do
(`service_access`), the credential check of a sign-in (`owner_sessions`).

A18: the daily run at 03:00 UTC while Registry runs with its tokens, from the
minute look and the dates the process remembers (rule 1); the copy, without
agent sessions, that `store` writes at the temporary path `backups` names
(rule 2), encrypted with the configured key, recording its
instant, release, last sequence number and key digest (rules 1, 3); the three
steps — removing temporary files, writing and checking the backup by
decrypting it and asking `store` to check the copy, deleting backups older
than 30 × 24 hours and unreadable ones (rule 4); the prefixes and the location
rules (rule 5), the probe file of A17 rule 2; the newest kept backup's instant
for the owner interface. No run in an owner-only start (rule 9).

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the configured addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2);
judgement.why: State 3 explicitly makes the probe file part of backups, forbids configuration from owning the probe, and makes instance_lifecycle order its invocation.
